prompt:
Use case: illustration-story.
Asset type: a high-resolution texture atlas of FOUR original decorative Chinese shadow-puppet illustrations for framed wall art in a heritage museum.
Layout is mandatory: a clean 2 by 2 grid of four equal rectangular illustrations, no gutters, no frames, no external margins. Overall landscape aspect ratio 3:2, each quadrant also 3:2. Each scene fills its entire own quadrant but keep important motifs 8 percent inside its quadrant edges. There must be NO line or decoration crossing between quadrants. The output is ONLY the flat artwork, front facing and orthographic, not a photograph of a room or a mockup.
Top left quadrant: an ornate red and jade Chinese shadow-puppet warrior on horseback, scalloped clouds and peonies; intricate cut-leather floral detailing and elegant silhouette.
Top right quadrant: three richly dressed Chinese shadow-puppet opera figures in profile beside a small traditional pavilion, theatrical gestures, graceful cloud scrolls.
Bottom left quadrant: poetic Jianghan-inspired river landscape, a small boat and fisherman, willow branches, lotus and distant tiled roofs, drawn in the same traditional shadow-puppet/folk-painting language, not a map.
Bottom right quadrant: an ornamental deer and phoenix amid peonies and curling cloud motifs, cut-paper and translucent painted leather patterns, harmonious lively composition.
Aesthetic: refined museum-quality traditional Chinese folk illustration, delicate pierced ornament, warm ivory handmade paper with restrained visible fibres, cinnabar red, rich jade and stone blue, soft ochre and muted antique gold, crisp very fine ink contours and clear pigment details. Vivid and layered but aged naturally, no distressed stains over the subjects. Include a fine restrained floral corner ornament INSIDE each illustration. Original themed imagery, no copies of identifiable historical artifacts. Uniform soft flat lighting, no cast shadows, no gradients suggesting 3D walls. No lettering, text, names, captions, digits, logos, watermarks or UI. Highest available detail; aim for a 3072 by 2048 pixel sheet without changing its 3:2 composition.
usage: Original decorative digital wall illustrations, not specific historical artifacts or performance stills. Mounted in physical wood and brass frames between and above the existing museum cabinets. A single atlas is sampled with per-plane UV coordinates; no full-screen overlay is used.

designStudy.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: photographic environment background for an existing interactive Chinese shadow-puppet museum website.
Input image 1 is the EDIT TARGET: the current finished long museum corridor with five cabinets. Edit this exact image in place, keeping its camera position, perspective, framing, image aspect ratio and all five cabinets in precisely the same positions and sizes. Preserve all windows, pendant lanterns, stone floor, doorways, cabinet contents, glass, and furniture. No people. The supplied corridor is currently too bare: enrich ONLY its exposed wall surfaces with beautifully installed Chinese shadow-puppetry illustrations.
Add a coherent collection of about six framed or mounted artworks following the receding corridor: an elegant tall illustrated silk/paper panel on the near left bare stone pier (it may be partially cropped by the left edge), a clearly visible beautifully framed vertical print in the blank plaster bay directly ABOVE the second cabinet, smaller companion prints on successive wall bays between windows above the distant cabinets, and two or three perspective-correct larger framed works on the visible RIGHT wall piers. Hang everything realistically on the actual wall planes, never across windows, over cabinet glass, in midair, or over the aisle. The illustrations should be exquisite Chinese folk shadow-puppet scenes, lively cut-leather profile figures with floral costumes, a small operatic scene, floral and cloud-pattern details. They are original themed digital illustrations, not copies of specific artifacts. Add restrained ornamental painted borders or a narrow patterned frieze on the same exposed plaster bays to make this feel like a carefully curated, richly decorated heritage gallery.
Materials: aged dark walnut frames, fine muted antique-gold inner edging, cream silk matting, printed pigment texture, red-brown hanging rails, real tiny contact shadows against weathered lime plaster. Rich cinnabar, lapis/stone blue, jade green, ochre, ivory and old gold in the art. Match existing amber lamps and cool blue evening window fill. The room should feel thoughtfully finished, warmer and more colorful, while retaining the believable old building patina.
Exact invariants: do not move or redraw any cabinet, do not change the five-cabinet spacing or outlines, do not add any new cabinets, do not move the windows, do not alter the crop or vanishing point, do not change room dimensions, keep the original stone texture and timber intact outside the added wall decorations. Maintain crisp deep focus, no haze, blur, bloom, global recoloring, waxy CG surfaces or game-render look. No readable lettering, no UI, numbers, labels, logos or watermark. Output the decorated corridor alone, at the highest available landscape resolution with fine crisp detail.
designStudy.usage: Color and framing study only; the earlier photographic corridor is not substituted for the current walkable 3D scene.
